title: Night ops debrief and SLO action items - May 03 2027
notes:
Summary:
Night shift observed a recurring tail-latency spike between 02:05–02:20 UTC on 2027-05-03 affecting the hosted API cluster in us-west-2. Error rates remained low (5xx at 0.2%) but P99 latency for text-generation routes increased from baseline ~210ms to peaks of ~1.8s. Incident surfaced as multiple SEV1 pager pages for high latency routing.

What happened (timeline):
- 02:02 UTC: Auto-scaling events completed; no capacity shortage in metrics.
- 02:05 UTC: First uptick in P95/P99 latency for /v1/generate observed (Dashboards: per-route > latency > generation).
- 02:07 UTC: On-call (Marcus) opened an incident bridge. Initial runbook checks (node health, GPU utilization) showed normal GPU load but an increase in small-batch requests.
- 02:10 UTC: Heap of KV-cache evictions detected on several serving nodes (logs: kv-cache.eviction). Eviction spikes correlated with a surge of short-sequence, high-concurrency requests from a single customer token bucket.
- 02:12 UTC: Automatic fallback routing engaged for some requests to cheaper model variants; this reduced error rate but did not fully restore tail latency.
- 02:18 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied — throttle policy adjusted for offending token bucket and prefix caching enabled for that customer where safe. Latency returned to ~250ms by 02:25 UTC.

Impact:
- Customer-facing failures: None critical (no increased 5xx), but elevated user-perceived latency for ~20min window across ~3% of requests in us-west-2. Estimated p99 token cost increase minimal; SLO: generation P99 target 300ms for prod routes; SLA breach avoided but SLO alert triggered.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Workload pattern: sudden burst of many small requests caused aggressive KV-cache churn on GPU serving nodes. Cache eviction stalls (metadata sync) introduced scheduling jitter and increased tail latency.
- Weakness in eviction heuristics: LRU preferred but per-tenant pressure can evict useful prefixes for other concurrent in-progress requests.
- Fallback routing and throttling logic worked but was reactive and required manual intervention to tune token bucket limits.

Immediate containment steps taken:
- Scoped throttle: increased token-bucket enforcement for the identified customer across us-west-2 (Marcus). Jira: SRE-4821 attached for tracking the throttle change.
- Enabled per-tenant safer prefix caching for the active customer where the model allowed structured caching (Priya).
- Short-lived increase in per-node KV-cache size by 15% to reduce evictions (Diego) — monitoring agreed to observe memory pressure.

Observations / telemetry to collect (actionable):
- Add a histogram of KV-cache eviction durations and eviction-related stall counts to the night-ops dashboard (metric name suggestions: kv_cache.eviction_duration_ms, kv_cache.eviction_stalls).
- Correlate token-bucket bursts to eviction spikes using request_id and tenant_id traces.
- Record exact sequence-length distribution during the 02:05 window for generation routes.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- SRE-4821 (Marcus) — finalize and deploy an automated temporary throttler that flips on when node-level eviction rate > 1000/min. ETA: 2027-05-10.
- Runbook update (Priya) — add a new checklist section for KV-cache eviction incidents: detection queries, quick containment knobs (per-tenant throttle, prefix-caching toggle, temporary cache size bump). ETA: 2027-05-07.
- Kernel/Runtime change (Diego) — prototype per-tenant cache partitions to prevent noisy neighbors evicting shared prefixes. Design doc PR: draft in progress, link in SRE ticket. ETA for prototype: 2027-06-01.
- Observability (Lina) — instrument eviction stalls and add alert rule: if eviction_stalls > 50 in 1m then page on-call and create incident. ETA: 2027-05-06.
- Post-incident customer communication (CS + SRE) — prepare a short explanation and risk mitigation note for affected accounts. Owner: Marcus + CS lead. ETA: 2027-05-05.

Runbook / playbook notes (quick reference):
- Initial checks: node health, GPU utilization, queue depth, KV-cache eviction rate, network egress.
- Quick mitigations (ordered): 1) Enable per-tenant prefix-caching if available, 2) Temporarily increase cache size (monitor memory), 3) Apply short-term per-tenant throttles, 4) Route to compatible model variant if latency persists.
- Documentation pointers: Confluence Night Operations Playbook -> KV-cache section.

Retrospective items for engineering planning:
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate high-churn small-request workloads to validate eviction heuristics. (Product & Runtime).
- Explore TTL-based caching for extremely short sequences to avoid unnecessary cache churn. (Research/Applied-ML).
- Revisit fallback routing aggressiveness: consider predictive routing when eviction rates trend up.

Handoff notes for day team (what to watch for in next 24–72h):
- Keep an eye on eviction_stalls metric and memory pressure after temporary cache size bump.
- Review the effect of the per-tenant throttle on customer experience; CS will flag if false positives visible.
- Verify that automated throttler in SRE-4821 is not too aggressive in the staging cluster.

Open questions / notes to self (work-in-progress style):
- Is full per-tenant cache partitioning feasible without a large memory overhead? Need memory model simulation.
- Could we prefer adaptive sampling for short sequences instead of caching them? Might reduce churn.
- Look into lightweight admission control at the front gate for high-concurrency small requests to smooth request bursts.

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot during incident):
- Generation route P50: 110ms -> unchanged.
- Generation route P95: 220ms -> peaked to 640ms.
- Generation route P99: 210ms -> peaked to 1800ms.
- 5xx rate: baseline 0.12% -> 0.20% during window.
- KV-cache eviction rate (per-node avg): baseline 12/min -> peaked 820/min.

Next steps:
- Triage meeting scheduled: 2027-05-04 10:00 UTC (invites sent). Required participants: Marcus, Priya, Diego, Lina, runtime lead.
- Draft a short post-incident note to share in SRE weekly. Responsible: Aisha (owner). ETA: 2027-05-06.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep this doc light — more detailed postmortem will be in SRE-4821 with logs and traces attached.
- Remember to escalate if similar pattern repeats in other regions (eu-west-1 next).

End of debrief.
